newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa to recognise Beijing, drop Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: South Africa to recognise Beijing, drop Taiwan.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela said on Wednesday South Africa was dropping recognition of Taiwan in favour of Beijing.
"We are now giving diplomatic recognition to the People's Republic of China and we are therefore downgrading relations with Taiwan," he told a news conference at his Johannesburg home.
He said it would be a gradual process he hoped could be completed within a year.
"A permanent continuation of diplomatic recognition of the Republic of China on (the island of) Taiwan is inconsistent with South Africa's role in international affairs," Mandela said.
Pretoria, whose white minority government had been a close ally of Taiwan while they were both shunned by international diplomacy, was the biggest of Taiwan's 30 diplomatic allies.
Beijing, which has China's seat at the United Nations, refuses to allow ties with any country that has diplomatic ties with Taipei.

Mandela, who said three months ago it would be "immoral" for him to drop Taipei, said South Africa's guiding diplomatic principle to the greater China region had been to seek cordial relations with both Chinas.

He expressed South Africa's great appreciation for Taiwan's engagement in South Africa and its assistance in the transition to democracy -- which included help to fund his election campaign -- and he hoped cordial relations would continue.

He met representatives of both Chinas on Tuesday and "expressed the hope that within the next 12 months it would be possible to achieve a smooth transition, acceptable to both the People's Republic of China and...Taiwan, in terms of which South Africa recognises the People's Republic of China but continues to conduct constructive relations with Taiwan".
Taiwan has major investments in South Africa but Pretoria has also been keen to improve trade links with mainland China.
